evidence: Did you get a chance to think it over on your end?
dimensions.tip: Probe deeper into caregiver turnover, billable-hour impact, and decision criteria instead of pivoting straight to product talk after one open question.

dimensions.label: Buying-signal detection & handling
evidence: What would it take to actually get this set up if we wanted to move forward?
dimensions.tip: When the prospect asks about setup/timeline, treat it as a buying signal and qualify budget, decision-maker involvement (Denise), and target start date rather than deflecting to 'send info.'

dimensions.label: Objection handling
evidence: We're a smaller shop though, only about 35 caregivers, so I don't know if we're the same scale as that 200-caregiver example.
dimensions.tip: Back up the 'scales down well' claim with a small-agency proof point or customer story instead of an unsupported assertion.

dimensions.label: Proof-point fidelity
evidence: One of our agency customers with around 200 caregivers told us Cally cut their missed check-in follow-ups dramatically
dimensions.tip: Use only published, specific Sensi metrics (e.g., 35% more billable hours, 300% retention) rather than vague anecdotal claims with no numbers.

dimensions.label: Next-step specificity
evidence: I'll shoot that over and we can regroup whenever you've had a chance to digest it.
dimensions.tip: Lock in a specific date/time for the follow-up call instead of an open-ended 'whenever you've had a chance.'

recommendations.why: Rep used vague anecdotal claims instead of citing Sensi's actual published metrics, weakening proof fidelity.

recommendations.title: Next-step commitment script/calendar template
recommendations.why: Call ended with a diffuse 'whenever' instead of a firm dated meeting, which risks stalling the deal further.

summary: The rep skipped genuine discovery and moved straight into a product pitch, missing the chance to explore Linda's specific pain points, budget, and timeline. Proof points were vague and anecdotal rather than tied to Sensi's published metrics, and the call closed with a soft, undated next step despite a clear buying signal ('what would it take to move forward').
